svg.title: Prezygotic and postzygotic barriers
svg.desc: Left box, prezygotic barriers, which act before a zygote forms: habitat isolation, living in different places and rarely meeting; temporal isolation, breeding at different times of day or year; behavioral isolation, mating songs or displays not recognized; mechanical isolation, reproductive parts do not fit; gametic isolation, sperm cannot fuse with the egg. An arrow leads to a circle labeled zygote forms, then to the right box, postzygotic barriers: hybrid inviability, the hybrid dies as an embryo or juvenile; hybrid sterility, the hybrid adult is sterile, as in a mule; hybrid breakdown, hybrids are fertile but their offspring are weak. Either kind blocks gene flow, so gene pools stay separate: reproductive isolation.

g.text: Reproductive barriers keep species apart, before and after a zygote forms
live in different places; rarely meet
breed at different times of day or year
mating songs or displays not recognized
sperm cannot fuse with the egg
hybrid dies as an embryo or juvenile
hybrids fertile, but their offspring weak
Either kind blocks gene flow between
populations, so their gene pools stay
